checks.note: Token page confirms OAuth2 client_credentials at /api/rest/v1/oauth/token, scopes data/user_management/publish/ri_import/backup, 900s bearer token, and the apiKey vs client_secret naming inconsistency. API key page confirms per-user key in profile. MCP auth page confirms OAuth 2.0 with .well-known discovery and no client ID/secret to configure.

API key page confirms the admin 'API' site area plus the user enabling a key in their profile, and says to contact the CSM. It says nothing on licensing, trial or sandbox. 'partner_gated' is an inference, not a vendor statement.

WebSocket is contradicted. The Publications page says events are polled ('continuous polling of the APIs'), with Poll and Acknowledge endpoints, and never mentions WebSocket. REST is only inferred from the docs, which contrast Publications with 'standard REST APIs'. Breadth 'broad' is supported by about 62 reference pages (Schema, Data, User Management, Publications, Backups, RI import).

An MCP server exists in the vendor's own docs under /mcp, so it is vendor-run (official). The cited URL is the docs section, not the endpoint. The connections page says the endpoint URL is tenant-specific and comes from your admin or Account Manager.

'blocked' is consistent with the other fields: no self-serve credentials, and an existing tenant and admin enablement are required. The blocker text should drop the WebSocket guess and the MCP URL remark.

corrected.one_liner: DealCloud (now part of Intapp) is a configurable CRM and deal/relationship management platform for financial services and professional services firms.
corrected.auth_notes: REST API: each user generates an API key (client id/secret) in their profile, exchanged at {site}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token via client_credentials with scopes (data, user_management, publish, ri_import, backup); bearer token lasts 900s, no refresh token. MCP server uses interactive per-user OAuth 2.0 with .well-known discovery; no client ID/secret to configure. The docs mix 'apiKey' and 'client_secret' wording, so that detail is unclear.
corrected.access_notes: No free or trial signup found. The API requires an existing DealCloud tenant (enterprise product). An admin must enable the 'API' site area for the user's group, then the user enables an API key in their profile. Docs point to the admin or Customer Success Manager for help. The docs do not say whether API access needs a specific license or add-on, and no public sandbox or free account was found. Classification as partner_gated is an inference from the enterprise-only product.
corrected.blocker: No self-serve way to get credentials: you need an existing DealCloud customer tenant and an admin to enable API access. Docs are public and the API is broad, so it is buildable for a customer. Publications (real-time events) are polled over the API (Poll/Acknowledge), not WebSocket. The MCP endpoint URL is tenant-specific and supplied by your admin or Account Manager; the cited URL is the docs section. Local MCP clients also need the Account Manager to enable the localhost redirect.
